The world's largest operator of the Boeing 737 family of aircraft, Southwest Airlines , continues to expand its US network, adding nonstop service from Fort Lauderdale (FLL) to San Diego (SAN) starting November 21. The hybrid airline will operate the city pair seasonally from November 21 through January 3.

Southwest's entry on this route will operate alongside another newcomer, JetBlue, which plans to fly the route from November 19. The only other airline operating between the two cities is Alaska Airlines , which has operated the route consistently since 2020.

Southwest Airlines Becomes The Third Operator Between Fort Lauderdale And San Diego

Starting on November 21, Southwest will become the third operator to fly between South Florida and San Diego. With Southwest joining JetBlue and Alaska, it marks the first time that three airlines have all operated the route at the same time.

Until 2016, there was no airline that had flown between Fort Lauderdale and San Diego, when JetBlue initially debuted on the route and operated the service up until January 2025. The route was then axed, but will return on a seasonal basis this winter.

Southwest will operate the route through early January. The service will begin as a three-weekly service, increasing to five weekly flights and then to daily by Christmas. The full schedule for the new seasonal service is as follows
A Short Southwest Seasonal Service To San Diego

Southwest has added the route between Fort Lauderdale and San Diego as part of its winter schedule to capture seasonal travel demand. This backfills capacity shifts for travel to South Florida, with the ultimate demise of Spirit Airlines (despite them not operating the route to San Diego).

This sees Southwest look for niche point-to-point additions on transcontinental markets. The schedule aligns with the current peak winter holiday demand and will operate in a travel window that can capture travelers across the Christmas break.

Passengers onboard will enjoy the airline's MAX 8 aircraft, operating a daytime service in each direction. San Diego remains a key facility for Southwest, with the airport remaining in the airline's top ten when analyzing Cirium data. Fort Lauderdale is another key market for the airline, with popular markets including Baltimore (BWI), Nashville (BNA), Chicago Midway (MDW), and St. Louis (STL).

西南航空成为劳德代尔堡和圣地亚哥之间的第三家运营商
从 11 月 21 日开始，西南航空将成为第三家在南佛罗里达和圣地亚哥之间运营航班的运营商。随着西南航空加入捷蓝航空和阿拉斯加航空的行列，这标志着三家航空公司首次同时运营该航线。
直到 2016 年，还没有任何航空公司运营过劳德代尔堡和圣地亚哥之间的航班，当时捷蓝航空最初开通了该航线，并运营该服务直至 2025 年 1 月。该航线后来被取消，但将于今年冬天按季节恢复。
西南航空将在一月初运营该航线。该服务将从每周三班开始，增加到每周五班，然后在圣诞节前增加到每天一班。新季节性服务的完整时间表如下

这使得西南航空在洲际市场上寻找利基点对点的新增服务。该时间表符合当前冬季假期的高峰需求，并将在一个可以吸引圣诞假期期间旅客的旅行窗口内运行。
机上乘客将享受该航空公司的 MAX 8 飞机，该飞机提供各个方向的日间服务。圣地亚哥仍然是西南航空的一个重要机场，在分析 Cirium 数据时，该机场仍名列该航空公司的前十名。劳德代尔堡是该航空公司的另一个重要市场，热门市场包括巴尔的摩 (BWI)、纳什维尔 (BNA)、芝加哥中途岛 (MDW) 和圣路易斯 (STL)。

title_en: BAE Systems raises cash flow outlook as GCAP, missile orders grow
title_zh: 随着 GCAP 和导弹订单的增长，BAE 系统公司提高了现金流前景
summary: BAE Systems has raised its free cash flow forecast for 2026 to about £3 billion ($4 billion), up… The post BAE Systems raises cash flow outlook as GCAP, missile orders grow appeared first on AeroTime .
summary_zh: BAE Systems 已将 2026 年自由现金流预测上调至约 30 亿英镑（40 亿美元）……
body_en: BAE Systems has raised its free cash flow forecast for 2026 to about £3 billion ($4 billion), up from its previous expectation of more than £2 billion ($2.7 billion), according to a market update published on November 12, 2026.

Customer advances have helped boost the figure. The revised forecast takes into account payments already received but excludes any large advances that could arrive before the end of the year. Such payments also contributed to the £1.79 billion ($2.4 billion) in free cash flow BAE Systems reported for the first half of 2026.

The company left its sales and earnings forecasts unchanged from July 2026. It still expects sales to grow by 8% to 10% from £30.7 billion ($40.7 billion) in 2025, underlying earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) by 10% to 12%, and underlying earnings per share (EPS) by 11% to 13%.
Business remained strong across Electronic Systems, Air, and Platforms & Services, helping offset weaker growth and margins in Maritime.
GCAP fighter contracts boost BAE Systems orders

BAE Systems said it had secured £33 billion ($43.8 billion) in orders so far in 2026 and expects further agreements before the end of the year. At the same stage in 2025, it had reported more than £27 billion ($35.8 billion) in orders.

The company booked about £1.6 billion ($2.1 billion) in orders related to the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP), including its share of the £4.6 billion ($6.1 billion) contract awarded to Edgewing in July 2026. Its share of MBDA orders added approximately £1.5 billion ($2 billion).

BAE Systems also listed a contract worth about A$1.3 billion ($890 million) for an Arctic over-the-horizon radar system Canada is buying from Australia. The Australian government valued the overall arrangement, signed on June 22, 2026, at A$2.5 billion ($1.7 billion) and described it as the country’s largest-ever defense export.

In the US, the company received about $1 billion (€900 million) in additional funding for munitions programs, including APKWS precision guidance systems and THAAD infrared seekers. It also received about $800 million (€720 million) to continue full-rate production of Armored Multi-Purpose Vehicles for the US Army.
Missile production and next-generation combat aircraft remain priorities
BAE Systems said it supports 10 of the 12 US munitions programs prioritized for significantly increased production capacity.

On March 25, 2026, it signed a seven-year framework agreement with the Pentagon to quadruple production capacity for the THAAD seeker it supplies to Lockheed Martin. In June 2026, Lockheed Martin received a contract worth up to $35 billion to quadruple THAAD interceptor output.

In the UK, BAE Systems pointed to the Defence Investment Plan published on June 30, 2026, which it said reinforces investment in next-generation fighters and autonomous collaborative combat aircraft. At the Farnborough International Airshow in July 2026, the company unveiled Brontanax , a self-funded collaborative combat aircraft prototype.

BAE Systems expects to return about £1.6 billion ($2.1 billion) to shareholders in 2026, including approximately £500 million ($660 million) in share buybacks. It will publish its full-year results on February 19, 2027.

body_zh: 根据 2026 年 11 月 12 日发布的市场更新，BAE Systems 将 2026 年自由现金流预测上调至约 30 亿英镑（40 亿美元），高于之前超过 20 亿英镑（27 亿美元）的预期。
客户的进步帮助提高了这一数字。修订后的预测考虑了已收到的付款，但不包括年底前可能到达的任何大额预付款。此类付款还为 BAE Systems 报告的 2026 年上半年自由现金流做出了 17.9 亿英镑（24 亿美元）的贡献。
该公司维持 2026 年 7 月的销售和盈利预测不变。仍预计 2025 年销售额将从 307 亿英镑（407 亿美元）增长 8% 至 10%，息税前基本利润 (EBIT) 增长 10% 至 12%，基本每股收益 (EPS) 增长 11% 至 13%。
电子系统、航空以及平台和服务业务保持强劲，有助于抵消海事领域增长和利润疲弱的影响。
GCAP战斗机合同增加了BAE系统公司的订单
BAE Systems 表示，截至 2026 年，该公司已获得 330 亿英镑（438 亿美元）的订单，并预计在年底前达成进一步协议。 2025 年同一阶段，该公司报告的订单金额超过 270 亿英镑（358 亿美元）。
该公司预订了约 16 亿英镑（21 亿美元）的与全球作战航空计划（GCAP）相关的订单，包括其在 2026 年 7 月授予 Edgewing 的 46 亿英镑（61 亿美元）合同中所占的份额。其在 MBDA 订单中的份额增加了约 15 亿英镑（20 亿美元）。
BAE系统公司还列出了加拿大从澳大利亚购买的价值约13亿澳元（合8.9亿美元）的北极超视距雷达系统合同。澳大利亚政府对 2026 年 6 月 22 日签署的总体安排的估值为 25 亿澳元（17 亿美元），并将其描述为该国有史以来最大的国防出口。
在美国，该公司获得了约 10 亿美元（9 亿欧元）的额外资金用于军需项目，包括 APKWS 精确制导系统和 THAAD 红外导引头。它还获得了约 8 亿美元（7.2 亿欧元），用于继续为美国陆军全速生产装甲多用途车辆。
导弹生产和下一代战斗机仍然是优先事项
BAE Systems 表示，它支持美国 12 个军火项目中的 10 个，这些项目优先考虑显着提高生产能力。
2026年3月25日，它与五角大楼签署了一项为期七年的框架协议，将其向洛克希德·马丁公司供应的“萨德”导引头的产能提高四倍。 2026 年 6 月，洛克希德·马丁公司获得了一份价值高达 350 亿美元的合同，将使“萨德”拦截弹的产量增加四倍。
在英国，BAE系统公司指出2026年6月30日发布的国防投资计划，称该计划加强了对下一代战斗机和自主协同战斗机的投资。在2026年7月的范堡罗国际航展上，该公司推出了自筹资金的协作战斗机原型机Brontanax。
BAE Systems 预计到 2026 年将向股东回报约 16 亿英镑（21 亿美元），其中包括约 5 亿英镑（6.6 亿美元）的股票回购。该公司将于2027年2月19日发布全年业绩。
随着 GCAP、导弹订单增长，BAE 系统公司上调现金流前景的消息首先出现在 AeroTime 上。

title_en: Cathay Pacific Orders 41 Airbus A330-900neos, As New Regional Workhorse
title_zh: 国泰航空订购 41 架空客 A330-900neos，作为新的区域主力
summary: Cathay Pacific has increased its Airbus A330-900neo order from 30 to 41 aircraft, which will replace older A330-300s and grow regional capacity, with deliveries from 2028 to 2035.
summary_zh: 国泰航空已将其空客 A330-900neo 订单从 30 架增加至 41 架，这将取代较旧的 A330-300 飞机并扩大区域运力，
body_en: In August 2024, Cathay Pacific placed an order for 30 Airbus A330neos . There’s now an update , as the airline has just bumped this order by 11 more planes, meaning that there are now a total of 41 of these aircraft on order. Let’s take a look at all the details, and discuss what this means for fleet modernization at the Hong Kong based oneworld carrier.
Cathay Group modernizing A330 fleet with A330-900neos
Cathay Pacific now has a firm order for 41 Airbus A330-900neo aircraft, which are expected to be delivered between 2028 and 2035.

This follows an evaluation of the carrier’s mid-size wide body fleet renewal program, and it will enable Cathay Pacific to modernize its earlier generation A330-300 fleet, and expand its operations on high capacity regional routes. However, the airline is leaving plans for this plane open, and also emphasizes how the jet offers the flexibility to serve longer range destinations.

For those not familiar, the A330neo is the updated version of the A330, featuring improved range and fuel efficiency. The A330-900neo is the larger of the two new variants (with the other being the A330-800neo). The plane has a range of 7,200 nautical miles, plus a capacity for 287 passengers in a standard three cabin configuration.

I think it’s safe to assume that at least most of these A330neos will be equipped with the new Aria Studio business class product , which is expected to be retrofitted on select existing A330s in the coming months. This will finally see the carrier introduce a dedicated regional product with flat beds, which is exciting, though it’s not quite to the level of the long haul Aria Suite business class .
Here’s how Cathay Pacific CEO Ronald Lam described how the A330neo fits into the carrier’s fleet, back when the first 30 frames were ordered

“The A330 is an aircraft type that has been serving Cathay Pacific well for nearly 30 years. These new aircraft will principally serve our regional destinations in Asia, while also providing the flexibility to serve longer-haul destinations as required. The improved fuel efficiency of these A330neos, together with their high standards of comfort, will enable us to further elevate the experience we provide for our customers while also contributing towards our goal of net-zero carbon emissions by 2050.”
How the A330neo fits into Cathay Pacific’s fleet

Cathay Pacific refreshing its short and medium haul fleet with the Airbus A330-900neo makes perfect sense, and is just about the safest, most expected aircraft order that Cathay Pacific could place. For context on Cathay Pacific’s fleet, the airline has
43 Airbus A330-300s, used primarily for regional routes, but also for some medium haul routes
54 Boeing 777s, most of which are long haul 777-300ERs, but there are also some regional 777-300s
48 Airbus A350s, split between the A350-900 and A350-1000 variant
Now Cathay Pacific’s fleet renewal plans are becoming a bit clearer, as the airline has
16 Airbus A321neos on order (beyond the ones already in the fleet), which will be used to expand regional capacity, and to introduce higher frequency service
41 Airbus A330-900neos on order, which will be used to replace the older A330-300s, and to also grow capacity in high demand regional markets
35 Boeing 777-9s on order , which will eventually be used as the carrier’s new flagship aircraft, replacing older 777s; these planes will feature a new first class and new business class product

So a decade down the road, you can expect that Cathay Pacific will primarily be flying A321neos, A330-900neos, A350s (-900s and -1000s), and 777-9s. That seems like a pretty logical fleet development plan to me.

Cathay Pacific now has an order for 41 Airbus A330-900neos, which the airline will primarily use to modernize and grow its regional fleet. The carrier already flies A330-300s, some of which are nearly 25 years old, so it’s logical that the airline would slowly be looking to replace these jets.
Cathay Pacific now has a pretty impressive (but not overly ambitious) order book, with A321neos, A330-900neos, and 777-9s, used for fleet renewal.
body_zh: 2024年8月，国泰航空订购了30架空客A330neo。现在有更新，因为该航空公司刚刚将该订单增加了 11 架飞机，这意味着现在总共订购了 41 架此类飞机。让我们看一下所有细节，并讨论这对香港寰宇一家航空公司的机队现代化意味着什么。
国泰集团使用 A330-900neos 现代化 A330 机队
国泰航空目前已获得41架空客A330-900neo飞机的确定订单，预计将于2028年至2035年期间交付。
这是在对该航空公司的中型宽体机队更新计划进行评估之后做出的，这将使国泰航空能够对其较早一代的 A330-300 机队进行现代化改造，并扩大其在高容量支线航线上的运营。然而，该航空公司尚未确定这架飞机的计划，并强调了这架飞机如何提供服务更远航程目的地的灵活性。
对于那些不熟悉的人来说，A330neo 是 A330 的更新版本，具有改进的航程和燃油效率。 A330-900neo 是两个新型号中较大的一个（另一个是 A330-800neo）。该飞机的航程为 7,200 海里，标准三舱配置可容纳 287 名乘客。
我认为可以肯定的是，至少大多数 A330neo 将配备新的 Aria Studio 商务舱产品，预计未来几个月将在部分现有 A330 上进行改装。这家航空公司最终将推出带有平板床的专用区域产品，这令人兴奋，尽管它还没有达到长途 Aria Suite 商务舱的水平。
以下是国泰航空首席执行官林中基描述 A330neo 如何融入国泰航空机队时，当时订购了首批 30 架飞机
“A330 是国泰航空近 30 年来一直提供良好服务的机型。这些新飞机将主要为我们在亚洲的支线目的地提供服务，同时也可根据需要灵活地为长途目的地提供服务。这些 A330neo 飞机提高的燃油效率及其高标准的舒适度将使我们能够进一步提升为客户提供的体验，同时也为我们到 2050 年实现净零碳排放的目标做出贡献。”
A330neo 如何融入国泰航空机队
国泰航空用空客 A330-900neo 更新其中短途机队是非常有意义的，也是国泰航空可能下的最安全、最令人期待的飞机订单。有关国泰航空机队的背景信息，该航空公司已
43 架空客 A330-300，主要用于支线航线，也用于一些中程航线
54 架波音 777，其中大部分是长途 777-300ER，但也有一些支线 777-300
现在，国泰航空的机队更新计划变得更加清晰，因为该航空公司已经
订购 16 架空客 A321neo（超出机队现有飞机），将用于扩大区域运力并引入更高频率的服务
订购 41 架空中客车 A330-900neos，将用于替换较旧的 A330-300，并增加高需求区域市场的运力
订购35架波音777-9，最终将用作该航空公司的新旗舰飞机，取代旧的777；这些飞机将配备新的头等舱和新的商务舱产品
因此，十年后，您可以预期国泰航空将主要使用 A321neos、A330-900neos、A350s（-900s 和 -1000s）和 777-9s 飞行。对我来说，这似乎是一个非常合乎逻辑的机队发展计划。
国泰航空目前已获得 41 架空客 A330-900neos 的订单，该航空公司将主要用这些飞机来实现其支线机队的现代化和发展。该航空公司已经运营 A330-300 飞机，其中一些机龄已近 25 年，因此该航空公司慢慢寻求更换这些飞机是合乎逻辑的。
国泰航空现在拥有令人印象深刻（但不是过于雄心勃勃）的订单，包括 A321neos、A330-900neos 和 777-9，用于机队更新。

title_en: Why Boeing 787-9 Airlines Face Different Maintenance Costs With Rolls-Royce & GE Engines
title_zh: 为什么波音 787-9 航空公司使用劳斯莱斯和 GE 发动机面临不同的维护成本
summary: Are the two engine options available for the 787-9 really that different in terms of cost? And what makes an airline decide between the two?
summary_zh: 787-9 的两种发动机选项在成本方面真的有那么大的不同吗？是什么让航空公司在两者之间做出选择？
body_en: Airline and Airport Management Graduate, Student Commercial Pilot and Commercial Aviation Writer.

Selecting a powerplant for a widebody fleet is one of the most consequential financial commitments an airline executive can make, locking the carrier into a multi-decade maintenance relationship that is quite tough to get out of. During the years where Boeing developed the Boeing 787 family, it made the decision to offer two distinct engine options, with the General Electric GEnx-1B and the Rolls-Royce Trent 1000. The dual-engine strategy successfully distributed supply chain risk and gave network planners purchasing leverage, but it also exposed airlines to vastly divergent operating economics and maintenance profiles.

Over the past decade, the operational histories of these two powerplants have gone on their own individual paths, driven by unexpected durability hurdles, time-on-wing variances, and costly fleet modifications. As a result, maintenance expenses can differ by millions of dollars per aircraft because of the engineering differences, repair liabilities, and long-term financial structures tied to each manufacturer.

Boeing's decision to engineer the 787 to accept two mutually exclusive engine types was rooted in lessons learned from earlier widebody programs. Offering both the General Electric GEnx-1B and the Rolls-Royce Trent 1000, Boeing wanted to show airlines that they no longer needed to be locked into a single supplier monopoly, but also to protect the airframer from production problems if one manufacturer faced factory delays. The flexibility allowed carriers to match engine performance characteristics to their specific route networks, balancing fuel burn against operating weights and thrust ratings.

The General Electric GEnx-1B is built on a twin-spool design featuring a carbon fiber composite fan and Twin Annular Pre-Swirl (TAPS) combustors, sharing operational lineage with engines powering larger Boeing aircraft. In contrast, the Rolls-Royce Trent 1000 is built on a signature three-shaft (triple-spool) configuration with intermediate-pressure stages and hollow titanium fan blades, designed exclusively for the Dreamliner family. These fundamental engineering differences meant that maintenance tooling, spare parts inventories, and overhaul procedures were entirely unique to each fleet type.

Over at the airlines, the choice initially came down to commercial inducements, leasing structures, and projected aircraft utilization. Airlines with heavy historical ties to Rolls-Royce naturally gravitated toward the Trent 1000 to maintain cross-fleet maintenance familiarity, while operators favoring General Electric chose the GEnx-1B for its established high-bypass efficiency. However, as aircraft accumulated operational flight hours, the underlying maintenance realities of each powerplant began to drift off in ways that reshaped global fleet orders.

The divergence in maintenance costs accelerated rapidly as early iterations of the Rolls-Royce Trent 1000 encountered intense, unforeseen durability hurdles. As noted by AirInsight , the powerplant's initial years in service were plagued by fatigue and corrosion issues within its intermediate-pressure turbine (IPT) blades, leading to accelerated wear and premature component failures. Although Rolls-Royce introduced the upgraded Trent 1000 TEN standard to resolve these issues, subsequent engineering evaluations showed that high-pressure turbine (HPT) blades were also wearing out significantly faster than projected design models anticipated.

What came was tough operational fallout for airlines flying Trent 1000-powered Dreamliners. It was immediate and severe, characterized by unexpected engine groundings, plummeting dispatch reliability, and soaring maintenance expenses. Major international operators such as Air New Zealand and British Airways were forced to ground aircraft for lengthy inspections and unscheduled overhauls, as reported by Aviation Week . To stick to already published flight schedules during these mandatory groundings, several affected carriers had to lease older, less fuel-efficient backup aircraft from the open market, incurring millions of dollars in supplementary operational expenses.

Airlines and their respective maintenance departments became reactionary, where engineers had to manage aggressive removal schedules and emergency component replacements well ahead of standard lifecycle intervals. While safety was rigorously maintained through constant borescope inspections and regulatory airworthiness directives, the financial toll of keeping these aircraft operational strained airline engineering budgets and disrupted long-term route planning.

The mechanical difficulties encountered by the Trent 1000 triggered profound financial consequences for Rolls-Royce and caused a noticeable shift in global widebody purchasing patterns. Industry reports from Aviation Week indicate that the cumulative cost of retrofits, customer compensation, and engine modifications surpassed $3 billion for Rolls-Royce, with aviation analysts estimating that up to 500 engines across the worldwide fleet needed remediation. The massive financial liability prompted corporate restructuring and an intensified engineering focus on redesigning hot-section components to restore customer confidence.

Concurrently, the maintenance disparity heavily influenced subsequent airline procurement decisions. Fleet data compiled by Simple Flying highlights a pronounced market shift: roughly 35% of the active Dreamliner fleet operates on Trent 1000 powerplants , while 65% relies on General Electric GEnx engines. In recent sales campaigns, widebody customers overwhelmingly selected GE, ordering 677 GEnx-powered aircraft compared to just 71 for the Trent 1000. Rolls-Royce's leadership, including engineering chief Simon Burr, candidly acknowledged that the company had surrendered market share because earlier iterations of the engine were simply not sufficiently durable.

That market contraction demonstrated how crucial predictable maintenance performance is to an aircraft's commercial success. Even though airlines frequently put pen to paper on aggressive initial acquisition discounts when finalizing engine selections, the long-term cost of unreliability and frequent shop visits quickly outweighs upfront savings, making durability the primary metric for fleet evaluation.

At the heart of widebody maintenance economics is the concept of time-on-wing, or the operational duration an engine can complete commercial flights before needing a major workshop overhaul. A General Electric GEnx-1B engine stays in the wing three times longer and can frequently achieve more than 20,000 operating hours before its first major shop visit, maintaining consistent fuel efficiency and low thermal stress. This extended durability significantly reduces the frequency with which an airline must unhang heavy powerplants from the wing and transport them to certified overhaul facilities.
body_zh: 航空公司和机场管理毕业生、商业飞行员学生和商业航空作家。
为宽体机队选择动力装置是航空公司高管可以做出的最重要的财务承诺之一，这使航空公司陷入了长达数十年的维护关系，而这种关系很难摆脱。在波音开发波音 787 系列飞机的那些年里，它决定提供两种不同的发动机选择，即通用电气 GEnx-1B 和劳斯莱斯遄达 1000。双发动机战略成功地分散了供应链风险，并为网络规划者提供了采购杠杆，但也让航空公司面临着截然不同的运营经济和维护状况。
在过去的十年中，这两个动力装置的运行历史在意想不到的耐用性障碍、在翼时间差异和昂贵的机队改装的推动下走上了各自的道路。因此，由于工程差异、维修责任和与每个制造商相关的长期财务结构，每架飞机的维护费用可能相差数百万美元。

波音公司决定对 787 进行设计以接受两种互斥的发动机类型，这一决定植根于从早期宽体项目中吸取的经验教训。波音公司同时提供通用电气 GEnx-1B 和劳斯莱斯遄达 1000 飞机，希望向航空公司表明，他们不再需要被单一供应商垄断，而且如果一家制造商面临工厂延误，也可以保护机身制造商免受生产问题的影响。这种灵活性使航空公司能够将发动机性能特征与其特定的航线网络相匹配，平衡燃油消耗与工作重量和推力额定值。
通用电气 GEnx-1B 采用双线轴设计，配有碳纤维复合材料风扇和双环形预旋流 (TAPS) 燃烧室，与为大型波音飞机提供动力的发动机共享运行谱系。相比之下，劳斯莱斯遄达 1000 采用标志性三轴（三线轴）配置，具有中压级和空心钛风扇叶片，专为梦想飞机系列设计。这些基本的工程差异意味着维护工具、备件库存和大修程序对于每种机队类型都是完全独特的。
对于航空公司来说，选择最初取决于商业诱因、租赁结构和预计的飞机利用率。与劳斯莱斯有着深厚历史渊源的航空公司自然会选择遄达 1000，以保持跨机队维护的熟悉程度，而青睐通用电气的运营商则选择 GEnx-1B，因为其既定的高旁路效率。然而，随着飞机运营飞行时间的增加，每个动力装置的基本维护现实开始发生变化，从而重塑了全球机队订单。

随着劳斯莱斯遄达 1000 的早期迭代遇到严重的、不可预见的耐用性障碍，维护成本的差异迅速扩大。正如 AirInsight 指出的那样，该动力装置在使用的最初几年受到中压涡轮 (IPT) 叶片疲劳和腐蚀问题的困扰，导致磨损加速和部件过早失效。尽管罗尔斯·罗伊斯推出了升级版的 Trent 1000 TEN 标准来解决这些问题，但随后的工程评估表明，高压涡轮 (HPT) 叶片的磨损速度也明显快于预计的设计模型预期。

对于使用遄达 1000 动力梦想飞机的航空公司来说，随之而来的是严峻的运营影响。这是直接而严重的，其特点是发动机意外接地、调度可靠性直线下降以及维护费用飙升。据《航空周刊》报道，新西兰航空和英国航空等主要国际运营商被迫停飞飞机进行长时间检查和计划外检修。为了在这些强制停飞期间遵守已经公布的航班时刻表，几家受影响的航空公司不得不从公开市场租赁较旧、燃油效率较低的备用飞机，从而产生了数百万美元的补充运营费用。
航空公司及其各自的维护部门变得保守，工程师必须在标准生命周期间隔之前管理积极的拆卸计划和紧急部件更换。虽然通过不断的管道镜检查和监管适航指令严格维护了安全性，但保持这些飞机运行的财务代价使航空公司工程预算紧张，并扰乱了长期航线规划。
遄达 1000 遇到的机械故障给劳斯莱斯带来了深远的财务影响，并导致全球宽体飞机采购模式发生显着变化。 《航空周刊》的行业报告显示，罗罗公司的改装、客户赔偿和发动机改装的累计成本超过 30 亿美元，航空分析师估计全球机队中有多达 500 台发动机需要修复。巨额财务负债促使公司进行重组，并加强工程重点，重新设计热部件，以恢复客户信心。

同时，维护差异严重影响了航空公司随后的采购决策。 Simple Flying 编制的机队数据凸显了明显的市场转变：大约 35% 的现役梦想飞机机队使用 Trent 1000 发动机，而 65% 则依赖通用电气 GEnx 发动机。在最近的销售活动中，宽体客机绝大多数选择了 GE，订购了 677 架 GEnx 动力飞机，而 Trent 1000 仅订购了 71 架。罗尔斯·罗伊斯的领导层，包括工程主管西蒙·伯尔 (Simon Burr)，坦率地承认，该公司已经放弃了市场份额，因为早期版本的发动机根本不够耐用。
市场萎缩表明，可预测的维护性能对于飞机的商业成功至关重要。尽管航空公司在最终确定发动机选择时经常在纸上写下激进的初始采购折扣，但不可靠性和频繁访问商店的长期成本很快就会超过前期节省，这使得耐用性成为机队评估的主要指标。
宽体机维护经济学的核心是在翼时间的概念，即发动机在需要进行大型车间大修之前可以完成商业飞行的运行持续时间。通用电气 GEnx-1B 发动机在机翼中的停留时间是原来的三倍，在首次大型维修前通常可以达到 20,000 多个运行小时，从而保持一致的燃油效率和低热应力。这种延长的耐用性大大降低了航空公司必须从机翼上卸下重型动力装置并将其运输到经过认证的检修设施的频率。

body_en: Two Cathay Pacific flights disrupted by technical issues - Aviation24.be

Two Hong Kong-bound Cathay Pacific flights were disrupted by technical issues on consecutive days. One returned to London Heathrow, while the other diverted to Osaka. Both aircraft landed safely, the airline told the South China Morning Post .

On Tuesday, 10 November, flight CX252 (Boeing 777-300ER reg. B-KPD, one world livery) made a precautionary return to London Heathrow after departing for Hong Kong. It landed at 14:23 local time, and passengers were rebooked on alternative flights.

On Wednesday, 11 November, flight CX521 from Tokyo Narita (Boeing 777-300 reg. B-HNE) diverted to Kansai International Airport in Osaka, where it landed at 19:00 local time. Passengers continued to Hong Kong on another Cathay Pacific aircraft (Airbus A330-300 reg. B-LAX). They arrived at destination with a delay of 5 hours and a quarter.
Cathay Pacific apologised to affected passengers. The airline did not specify the nature of either technical issue in the account reported by the South China Morning Post .

title_en: The Boeing 737 NG Still Has Years Of Flying Left, But Its Largest Operator Doesn't Want It Anymore
title_zh: 波音 737 NG 仍有多年飞行时间，但其最大的运营商不再想要它
summary: The 737 NG is still highly in favor by many carriers around the world, but the prospect of the MAX effect is too big to ignore for Southwest
summary_zh: 737 NG仍然受到全球许多航空公司的青睐，但MAX效应的前景对西南航空来说不容忽视
body_en: Airline and Airport Management Graduate, Student Commercial Pilot and Commercial Aviation Writer.

The symbiotic relationship between Southwest Airlines and the Boeing 737 Next Generation family has defined the very essence of low-cost domestic travel. Operating hundreds of Boeing 737-700 and Boeing 737-800 aircraft, the carrier built its legendary point-to-point network around the reliability, commonality, and rugged versatility of Boeing’s popular narrowbody workhorse. These airframes logged millions of flight hours, connecting passengers across thousands of city pairs while fostering an operational culture deeply rooted in single-type fleet efficiency.

During its September 2024 Investor Day, Southwest made a decision that stunned industry observers: a firm commitment to retire all 571 Next Generation aircraft by the end of 2031 in favor of an all-MAX fleet. This decision comes even though many of these airframes retain substantial structural and calendar life and can fly for years to come. The move is part of a profound evolution in modern airline fleet planning, where superior fuel efficiency, reduced emissions, and higher seating capacity outweigh the mechanical longevity of mature narrowbody types.

It cannot be overstated how significant Southwest's pivot is, especially given the sheer scale of the fleet involved in this generational transition. Operating 450 Next Generation aircraft consisting of 262 737-700s and 188 737-800s in active service, according to ch-aviation . Southwest is the largest operator of the type in global aviation, by some distance. These aircraft have been the fundamental building blocks of the airline's dense domestic schedules, operating multiple short-to-medium-haul legs daily with exceptional dispatch reliability.

The cornerstone of the 2031 roadmap is a dramatic rejuvenation of the carrier's asset profile, designed to bring down the average age of its operating fleet from approximately 11.5 years to just 5 years, as reported by Airline Geeks . By replacing older NG variants with new Boeing 737 MAX 8 and upcoming MAX 7 airframes, Southwest aims to modernize its operational footprint while enhancing environmental performance.

Completing a retirement campaign of this scale will not come without its challenges, especially in managing manufacturer delivery schedules, regulatory certifications, and network capacity demands. While the end-of-2031 target provides a clear strategic horizon, executive leadership has acknowledged that the exact pace remains tethered to Boeing's delivery cadence and certification timelines for smaller variant types. Consequently, while the ultimate destination is an all-MAX operational model, the winding down of the Next Generation era will be a methodical, multi-year process.

The underlying justification for moving away from the 737 Next Generation family centers entirely on modern thermodynamic efficiency and seating economics. When Southwest introduced the 737 MAX 8 into active service, manufacturer projections indicated a fuel burn reduction of approximately 14% compared to the NG airframes . In operational practice, Southwest annual reports have consistently credited fleet-wide fuel savings to the strategic integration of MAX aircraft alongside the systematic retirement of older 737-700s, turning environmental efficiency into a powerful bottom-line advantage.

A standard Southwest 737-700 accommodates 143 passengers in a single-class configuration, whereas the larger MAX 8 expands capacity to 175 passengers. This density gain allows the carrier to generate significantly higher revenue per departure on high-demand trunk routes without increasing aircraft count or slot footprint at congested airports. Ultimately, the economic performance gap between NG and MAX equipment becomes insurmountable for long-term fleet planning because of the higher passenger counts with lower fuel burn per seat.

Transitioning away from legacy NGs enables Southwest to compress its average fleet age, with benefits that may not seem obvious at first. Operating a substantially younger aircraft family slashes unscheduled maintenance events, reduces component replacement costs, and enhances schedule reliability across thousands of daily departures. The airframes of the older generation are still airworthy, but the sheer financial velocity of MAX-generation operating margins makes retaining the older fleet commercially unjustifiable.

Embarking on a fleet transition of this magnitude, however, is heavily constrained by external aerospace supply chains and manufacturer delivery cadences. Southwest originally outlined an ambitious target to phase out all Next Generation aircraft by the end of 2031, but the pace of this retirement campaign is intrinsically tied to Boeing's ability to roll out new single-aisle jets from its assembly lines. Supply chain issues, regulatory scrutiny, and production-rate adjustments have repeatedly pushed carriers worldwide to recalibrate their fleet retirement horizons.

Recent operational cadences illustrate the delicate equilibrium needed between retirements and incoming deliveries. For instance, the airline retired 55 Next Generation aircraft in 2025, comprising 48 737-700s and 7 737-800s, while taking delivery of 55 new MAX 8 airframes, followed by planned schedules for roughly 66 MAX deliveries and 60 retirements in subsequent operating cycles, as per data from Cranky Flier . Annual delivery volumes fluctuate based on OEM manufacturing stability, so matching retirements one-to-one with new arrivals is a complex logistical challenge for fleet planners.

Consequently, executive leadership has adopted a pragmatic stance regarding the timeline's rigidity. Chief Financial Officer Tom Doxey noted that Southwest still maintains more than 450 Next Generation airframes that will be phased out gradually for years to come, well into the next decade, according to Aviation Week . Of course, the 2031 target is the ultimate strategic horizon, but aircraft production backlogs will likely extend the twilight of the 737 NG era beyond initial projections.

Southwest Airlines is aggressively shedding its Next Generation fleet to the point that the existing fleet seems far too outdated, though these airframes are far from obsolete and still have robust demand across the secondary global market. Regional carriers, leasing companies, and growing airlines eagerly queue for surplus 737-700 and 737-800 units, allowing Southwest to capitalize on strong secondhand asset valuations . Southwest is focused on monetizing select airframes and surplus spare engines while market conditions remain highly favorable.
body_zh: 航空公司和机场管理毕业生、商业飞行员学生和商业航空作家。
西南航空与下一代波音 737 系列之间的共生关系定义了低成本国内旅行的本质。该航空公司运营数百架波音 737-700 和波音 737-800 飞机，围绕波音广受欢迎的窄体机的可靠性、通用性和坚固耐用的多功能性构建了传奇的点对点网络。这些机身记录了数百万小时的飞行时间，连接了数千个城市对的乘客，同时培育了一种根植于单一机队效率的运营文化。
在 2024 年 9 月的投资者日期间，西南航空做出了一项令行业观察人士震惊的决定：坚定承诺在 2031 年底前退役所有 571 架下一代飞机，转而采用全 MAX 机队。尽管这些机身中的许多都保留了相当长的结构和日历寿命并且可以在未来几年飞行，但还是做出了这一决定。此举是现代航空公司机队规划深刻演变的一部分，其中卓越的燃油效率、减少的排放和更高的座位容量超过了成熟窄体机类型的机械寿命。
西南航空的转型意义重大，怎么强调都不为过，特别是考虑到参与这一代际过渡的机队规模庞大。据 ch-aviation 称，运营着 450 架下一代飞机，其中包括 262 737-700 架和 188 737-800 架现役飞机。西南航空是全球航空业中最大的此类运营商，在一定程度上遥遥领先。这些飞机一直是该航空公司密集的国内航班时刻表的基本组成部分，每天运营多个中短程航班，并具有卓越的调度可靠性。
据 Airline Geeks 报道，2031 年路线图的基石是大幅振兴该航空公司的资产状况，旨在将其运营机队的平均机龄从约 11.5 年缩短至仅 5 年。通过用新型波音 737 MAX 8 和即将推出的 MAX 7 机身替换旧的 NG 机型，西南航空旨在实现运营足迹现代化，同时提高环境绩效。
完成如此规模的退役活动不会没有挑战，特别是在管理制造商交付计划、监管认证和网络容量需求方面。虽然 2031 年底的目标提供了明确的战略视野，但执行领导层承认，确切的速度仍然取决于波音公司较小型号飞机的交付节奏和认证时间表。因此，虽然最终目标是全 MAX 运营模式，但下一代时代的结束将是一个有条不紊的、多年的过程。
放弃 737 下一代系列的根本理由完全集中在现代热力学效率和座椅经济性上。当西南航空将 737 MAX 8 投入现役时，制造商预测表明与 NG 机身相比，燃油消耗减少约 14%。在运营实践中，西南航空的年度报告一致将整个机队的燃油节省归功于 MAX 飞机的战略整合以及老旧 737-700 的系统退役，将环境效率转化为强大的底线优势。
标准西南航空 737-700 的单舱配置可容纳 143 名乘客，而较大的 MAX 8 则可将载客量扩展至 175 名乘客。这种密度增益使航空公司能够在高需求干线航线上的每次出发产生显着更高的收入，而无需增加拥挤机场的飞机数量或起落架占地面积。最终，NG 和 MAX 设备之间的经济性能差距对于长期机队规划而言变得难以克服，因为乘客数量较多，而每个座位的燃油消耗较低。
摆脱传统NG 使西南航空能够压缩其平均机队机龄，其好处乍一看可能并不明显。运营更年轻的飞机系列可以减少计划外维护事件，降低部件更换成本，并提高每日数千次出发的计划可靠性。老一代的机身仍然适航，但 MAX 一代运营利润的巨大财务速度使得保留老旧机队在商业上不合理。
然而，如此大规模的机队转型受到外部航空航天供应链和制造商交付节奏的严重限制。西南航空最初制定了一个雄心勃勃的目标，即到 2031 年底逐步淘汰所有下一代飞机，但这一退役计划的步伐本质上与波音从其装配线推出新型单通道喷气式飞机的能力相关。供应链问题、监管审查和生产率调整一再促使世界各地的航空公司重新调整其机队退役期限。

最近的运营节奏说明了退役和即将交付之间所需的微妙平衡。例如，根据 Cranky Flier 的数据，该航空公司将在 2025 年退役 55 架下一代飞机，其中包括 48 737-700 架和 7 737-800 架，同时接收 55 架新 MAX 8 机身，随后计划在后续运营周期中交付约 66 架 MAX 并退役 60 架。年度交付量根据 OEM 制造稳定性而波动，因此将退役产品与新产品一对一匹配对于车队规划者来说是一项复杂的后勤挑战。
因此，行政领导层对时间表的严格性采取了务实的立场。据《航空周刊》报道，首席财务官汤姆·多克西 (Tom Doxey) 指出，西南航空仍保留着 450 多架下一代机身，这些机身将在未来几年甚至下一个十年内逐步淘汰。当然，2031 年的目标是最终的战略视野，但飞机生产积压可能会延长 737 NG 时代的黄昏，超出最初的预测。
西南航空正在积极削减其下一代机队，以至于现有机队似乎已经过时了，尽管这些机身远未过时，并且在全球二级市场仍然有强劲的需求。支线航空公司、租赁公司和成长型航空公司急切地等待剩余的 737-700 和 737-800 架飞机，使西南航空能够利用强劲的二手资产估值。西南航空专注于将选定的机身和过剩的备用发动机货币化，同时市场状况仍然非常有利。

title_en: 8 Things Frequent Flyers Do Differently To Survive Long-Haul Flights
title_zh: 为了在长途飞行中生存下来，飞行常客会采取不同的 8 件事
summary: Long-haul flights are taxing at the best of times, but there are ways to improve the experience.
summary_zh: 即使在最好的情况下，长途飞行也会很费力，但有一些方法可以改善体验。
body_en: Based in the UK, Josh is a keen writer with a degree in Military History. Having worked previously as a financial journalist, he has covered the aviation industry extensively, reporting on airlines' results and monthly passenger statistics in the aftermath of the pandemic, alongside the likes of regulation around sustainable fuels, and the prospects for hydrogen-powered commercial flight. He joins Simple Flying with a lifelong love of all things aviation.

Long-haul flying can be taxing at the best of times. Prolonged exposure to reduced air pressure and low humidity in cabins, as well as lengthy periods of immobility and sleep disruption, all take their toll on the body. Even if one factor can be prevented by flying on a premium fare, chances are the effects of another will catch up to passengers.

But there are things travelers can do to mitigate the impacts of spending so long in such conditions. A long-haul flight does not have to be completely unbearable, of course. Preparation ahead of time is key. Here, we highlight some of the tricks frequent flyers use to survive long-haul flights.
For the best chance of space to sleep or access to room to move around.

Although it may sound obvious, getting a seat reservation in sooner rather than later ensures a desired spot and, most importantly, reduces the chance of being stuck in a dreaded middle seat. The majority of airlines let their passengers pick a specific seat or seats well before their flight departs. The caveat is, doing so may come at an additional cost.

Airlines on the whole have increasingly taken to charging passengers extra for seat selection as a means to generate additional revenue. The alternative in many cases is to wait until check-in opens, the timing of which can depend on fare class and type, and be assigned a seat by the airline or choose from what is left at no additional cost. Bear in mind, policies vary carrier to carrier, so it is always worth checking how the specific airline treats booking and seat selection ahead of time.

That said, generally speaking, travelers get the option of either saving money and losing out on being able to pick their own spot onboard, or forking out a bit extra for the choice. On long-haul flights, the question to ask is how important sitting in the right area is. If possible in the cabin attached to a fare, sitting forward of the engines can mean a quieter journey, for instance. Similarly, being next to a window allows that bit of extra space, while direct aisle access means the choice of standing up and moving about the cabin if and when one pleases.
Easy access to essentials can be a game-changer mid-flight.

Once onboard, having easy access to anything that may be needed during the flight is vital. An easy way to ensure this is by separating such essentials into a smaller bag or kit that can be removed from carry-on luggage and kept handy at the seat. That, in turn, means the carry-on can remain in overhead storage and free up legroom.

As to what to pack in this kit, everyone will have their preferences. Generally speaking, though, device chargers, an eye mask, and toiletries all come in useful . Tod Covich, travel director at tour company Trafalgar , also previously flagged the likes of a reusable water bottle, lip balm, toothbrush, snacks, and compression socks as among his own essentials.
Long-haul flight essentials, from Trafalgar’s Tod Covich
*Some airlines restrict the use of portable chargers onboard

Any means of staying and feeling cleansed during long-haul journeys can go a long way to adding to one's sense of wellbeing. Bringing snacks, too, means some choice over when to eat rather than meal times being fully determined by the airline.
Constant exposure to background noise is known to drain energy.

Although somewhat encompassed within the kit of essentials to keep handy on a flight, noise-canceling headphones deserve their own honorable mention. Constant background noise is proven to drain energy and contribute to fatigue during long-haul journeys, so any means of drowning it out is worth considering.

Where airlines offer in-flight entertainment, complimentary headphones are usually included. Anyone who has traveled long-haul will tell you that the quality of these can leave much to be desired. Although some airlines may surprise in this sense, the risk is arguably not one worth taking.

For reference, Singapore Airlines, British Airways, Delta Air Lines, and All Nippon Airways (ANA) are among a score of carriers that do in fact supply noise-canceling headphones. This tends to be the case for premium passengers, though, meaning the chances of being offered the technology in economy are incredibly low, regardless of carrier.
No harm in backup options to in-flight entertainment.

Headphones and inflight entertainment go hand in hand. There is no point in trying to watch a movie or listen to music if a headset does nothing to drown out the noise of a plane’s engines or enclosed cabin environment, of course. Alternatively, having a suitable means to hear the likes of movies or music is pointless if the entertainment itself is not suited to your tastes.

The solution: Bring backup entertainment. Anything from a book to songs, movies, or a series downloaded on a personal device can stave off boredom once and for all. Boredom itself is part and parcel of flying long-haul, particularly among younger travelers.
body_zh: 乔什居住在英国，是一位热心作家，拥有军事史学位。此前，他曾担任财经记者，广泛报道了航空业，报道了疫情后航空公司的业绩和每月乘客统计数据，以及可持续燃料的监管以及氢动力商业航班的前景等。他带着对航空一切事物的终生热爱加入了 Simple Flying。
即使在最好的情况下，长途飞行也会很费力。长时间暴露在机舱内气压低、湿度低的环境中，以及长时间不动和睡眠中断，都会对身体造成损害。即使可以通过高价飞行来避免一个因素，但另一个因素的影响很可能会影响到乘客。
但旅行者可以采取一些措施来减轻在这种情况下花费这么长时间的影响。当然，长途飞行并不一定是完全难以忍受的。提前做好准备是关键。在这里，我们重点介绍常旅客在长途飞行中生存的一些技巧。
获得最佳的睡眠空间或活动空间。
虽然这听起来似乎是理所当然的事情，但尽早预订座位可以确保获得理想的座位，最重要的是，可以减少被困在可怕的中间座位的机会。大多数航空公司会让乘客在航班起飞前选择一个或多个特定座位。需要注意的是，这样做可能会产生额外费用。
总体而言，航空公司越来越多地向乘客收取额外选座费用，以此作为创造额外收入的手段。在许多情况下，另一种选择是等到办理登机手续开始，办理登机手续的时间可能取决于票价舱位和类型，然后由航空公司分配座位或从剩余座位中选择座位，无需支付额外费用。请记住，各航空公司的政策各不相同，因此始终值得提前检查特定航空公司如何对待预订和座位选择。
也就是说，一般来说，旅客可以选择要么省钱，但失去在船上选择自己的位置的机会，要么多花一点钱来选择。在长途航班上，要问的问题是坐在正确的区域有多重要。例如，如果可能的话，在附有票价的机舱内，坐在发动机前面可能意味着更安静的旅程。同样，靠近窗户可以提供一点额外的空间，而直接进入过道意味着可以在愿意的时候选择站起来并在机舱内走动。
在飞行途中轻松获取必需品可能会改变游戏规则。
登机后，轻松获取飞行期间可能需要的任何物品至关重要。确保这一点的一个简单方法是将这些必需品分成一个较小的袋子或套件，可以从随身行李中取出并放在座位上方便取用的地方。反过来，这意味着随身行李可以保留在头顶储物空间中，从而腾出腿部空间。
至于这个套件里装什么，每个人都会有自己的喜好。不过，一般来说，设备充电器、眼罩和洗漱用品都很有用。特拉法尔加旅游公司的旅行总监托德·科维奇此前也表示，可重复使用的水瓶、润唇膏、牙刷、零食和压力袜等都是他自己的必需品。
长途飞行必备品，来自特拉法加的 Tod Covich
*部分航空公司限制在机上使用便携式充电器
在长途旅行中任何停留和感觉净化的方式都可以大大增加一个人的幸福感。携带零食也意味着可以选择何时进食，而不是完全由航空公司决定用餐时间。
众所周知，持续暴露在背景噪音中会消耗能量。
尽管降噪耳机在某种程度上包含在飞行时随身携带的必需品套件中，但它值得一提。事实证明，在长途旅行中，持续的背景噪音会消耗能量并导致疲劳，因此任何消除噪音的方法都值得考虑。
如果航空公司提供机上娱乐服务，通常会提供免费耳机。任何经历过长途旅行的人都会告诉您，这些产品的质量还有很多不足之处。尽管一些航空公司可能会在这个意义上感到惊讶，但可以说这种风险并不值得冒。
作为参考，新加坡航空、英国航空、达美航空和全日空航空 (ANA) 等多家航空公司确实提供降噪耳机。不过，对于高级乘客来说，情况往往如此，这意味着无论哪家航空公司，在经济舱中获得该技术的机会都非常低。
备份选项对机上娱乐没有任何损害。
耳机和机上娱乐齐头并进。当然，如果耳机无法掩盖飞机引擎或封闭机舱环境的噪音，那么尝试看电影或听音乐就没有意义。或者，如果娱乐本身不适合您的口味，那么拥有合适的方式来聆听电影或音乐等内容就没有意义。
解决方案：带上备用娱乐设施。从书籍到歌曲、电影或在个人设备上下载的连续剧，任何东西都可以一劳永逸地消除无聊。无聊本身就是长途飞行的重要组成部分，尤其是对于年轻旅行者来说。

title_en: Four killed in Turkish military S-70 helicopter crash
title_zh: 土耳其军用S-70直升机坠毁造成四人死亡
summary: Four Turkish service members died when a military Sikorsky S-70 helicopter crashed on the outskirts of Malatya in… The post Four killed in Turkish military S-70 helicopter crash appeared first on AeroTime .
summary_zh: 一架西科斯基 S-70 军用直升机在马拉蒂亚郊区坠毁，四名土耳其军人死亡……四名土耳其军人丧生
body_en: Four Turkish service members died when a military Sikorsky S-70 helicopter crashed on the outskirts of Malatya in eastern Turkey on November 12, 2026, the country’s Defense Ministry said.

The helicopter came down at about 18:45 local time in a neighborhood in Malatya’s Yeşilyurt district, according to local media. Police, firefighters and medical teams responded to the crash. Footage aired by Turkish broadcasters showed flames and smoke rising from the wreckage as emergency vehicles gathered nearby.
The Defense Ministry said it had yet to determine what caused the crash. Its initial statement identified the aircraft as an S-70 but gave no details about the mission or the roles of those aboard.
The Malatya chief public prosecutor’s office opened an investigation into the crash. A deputy chief prosecutor and two prosecutors have been assigned to the case, Turkey’s Anadolu Agency reported.

Turkey has operated Sikorsky Black Hawk helicopters for decades. Its armed forces already had more than 100 UH-60s in service in 2016, when Sikorsky and Turkish Aerospace Industries launched a program to build a version of the S-70i domestically under license.
The Turkish-built helicopter carries the designation T70. The program calls for 109 helicopters for six military and civilian operators, including Turkey’s land forces, air force and gendarmerie.
Turkish Aerospace delivered the first T70 to the gendarmerie in late 2022. The original order also included 20 helicopters configured for firefighting for Turkey’s forestry service.

body_zh: 土耳其国防部表示，2026 年 11 月 12 日，一架西科斯基 S-70 军用直升机在土耳其东部马拉蒂亚郊区坠毁，造成 4 名土耳其军人死亡。
据当地媒体报道，直升机于当地时间 18 点 45 分左右在马拉蒂亚 Yeşilyurt 区的一个社区坠毁。警察、消防员和医疗队对事故做出了反应。土耳其广播公司播放的视频显示，紧急车辆聚集在附近，残骸中冒出火焰和浓烟。
国防部表示，尚未确定坠机原因。其最初的声明将这架飞机确定为 S-70，但没有提供有关任务或机上人员角色的详细信息。
马拉蒂亚首席检察官办公室对这起事故展开调查。据土耳其阿纳多卢通讯社报道，一名副首席检察官和两名检察官已被指派处理此案。
土耳其几十年来一直运营西科斯基黑鹰直升机。 2016 年，西科斯基和土耳其航空航天工业公司启动了一项计划，根据许可在国内生产 S-70i 版本，其武装部队已有 100 多架 UH-60 服役。
这架土耳其制造的直升机的代号为 T70。该计划需要为土耳其陆军、空军和宪兵等六家军事和民用运营商提供 109 架直升机。
土耳其航空航天公司于 2022 年底向宪兵队交付了第一架 T70。最初的订单还包括 20 架配置用于土耳其林业部门消防的直升机。
在土耳其军用 S-70 直升机坠毁事件中丧生的四号员首先出现在 AeroTime 上。

title_en: Do You Know? The World's Busiest Airport Has No Flights To These 2 US States
title_zh: 你知道吗？世界上最繁忙的机场没有飞往美国这两个州的航班
summary: A global flight hub linking 257 cities while unexpected domestic gaps linger due to history, demand and nearby hubs.
summary_zh: 一个连接 257 个城市的全球航空枢纽，而由于历史、需求和附近枢纽的原因，意外的国内差距仍然存在。
body_en: Journalist – Aaron is an aviation and travel journalist with 14 years of experience in the travel and tourism industry. His background spans airport operations, aviation infrastructure, and travel consulting, having worked with global organizations across New Zealand, Europe, and North America.

Combining industry expertise with firsthand travel experience across more than 52 countries and five continents, Aaron covers airlines, airports, aviation policy, and the wider travel sector. He is based in Canterbury, New Zealand.
His work has been published in Simple Flying and featured by MSN, SAM CHUI Aviation & Travel, EIN News, Pakistan Defence, and Climate Depot.

Chicago O'Hare International Airport (ORD) is the world's busiest airport by the number of flights, and it has international and domestic operators providing nonstop services across the globe. At home, in the US, the airport provides nonstop flights to almost every state, with just Delaware and Mississippi missing from its route map.

Using data from Cirium , an online aviation analytics company, Simple Flying analyzed the airport's network from Chicago O'Hare and understands why the airport is missing its last two links to a full domestic network.

No Flights From Chicago O'Hare To Mississippi

Chicago O'Hare is the busiest airport in the world , ahead of the likes of Atlanta (ATL), Dubai (DXB) and London Heathrow (LHR) when looking at the total number of flights operated. Evidently, by passengers served, Atlanta takes the crown for the busiest airport, while Dubai is the world's leading international airport.

Travelers bound for the US states of Delaware or Mississippi are out of luck for nonstop flights from O'Hare, with no airlines operating. The last time an airline flew to Mississippi from O'Hare was American Airlines , which last flew to the southern state in 2020.

American Airlines historically flew from O'Hare to Jackson in 2006 to 2007, and then to Gulfport between 2007 and 2008. American returned in 2017 with flights to Meridian, which were then withdrawn in 2020. The airline then ultimately withdrew from serving the state. United Airlines also flew to Mississippi from 2012 through 2020, and has not returned since the COVID-19 pandemic.
Delaware Remains Unconnected To The Windy City
Reviewing history back to the beginning of the 1990s, Delaware has never had a regular nonstop service to Chicago O'Hare. Even neighboring Chicago Midway (MDW) has no nonstop flights to the state.

Delaware is a small state on the US East Coast, neighboring New Jersey, Maryland, and Pennsylvania. Wilmington, the largest city in the state, is less than an hour's drive from Philadelphia International Airport (PHL), seeing the majority of travelers looking to travel head to this major airport. Delaware is also within driving distance of Baltimore (BWI), which is a major Southwest hub.

Aaron 将行业专业知识与五大洲超过 52 个国家/地区的第一手旅行经验相结合，涵盖航空公司、机场、航空政策和更广泛的旅行领域。他居住在新西兰坎特伯雷。
他的作品发表在《Simple Flying》上，并受到 MSN、SAM CHUI Aviation & Travel、EIN News、Pakistan Defence 和 Climate Depot 的专题报道。

body_en: James lives and breathes route development. Educated in Air Transport Management at Loughborough University and Cranfield University, James has a PhD in Airline Strategy and Economics. James was Market Opportunity Analyst at London Luton Airport and Chief Analyst at anna.aero. He taught airline strategy and economics to undergraduate and postgraduate students for five years and has worked closely with multiple carriers on route and market intelligence projects. He is based near London, UK.

All airlines have route churn, and Air Canada is no exception. When the Star Alliance member's overall network is explored, ten routes that operated during the summer are not scheduled to return in 2027. Eight are international and two are domestic.

Air Canada is overwhelmingly the country's largest operator. OAG data for 2026 shows that it has 30% of domestic flights (WestJet is second with 21%) and 37% for the overall international arena (WestJet follows with 14%). For long-haul activity, Air Canada has 38% of the market ( Air Transat is second with 11% ).
Air Canada Has Pulled These Eight International Routes

They all had flights at some point between May 2026 and January 2027, but no service is scheduled thereafter . The entries include Vancouver to Singapore , which is currently the airline's longest nonstop operation. The final departure will leave British Columbia on January 24, 2027.

That link's axing was probably influenced by the high price of fuel, which worsens the economics of ultra-long-haul routes. The situation may also put a damper on any other ultra-long markets that Air Canada was considering announcing. This might have included Ho Chi Minh City , following Canada and Vietnam recently expanding their bilateral air service agreement and much speculation .

Other eliminated routes included the thin links from Vancouver to Nashville and Raleigh-Durham, with Air Canada's flights only lasting for two seasons. It was the first time that British Columbia had nonstop service to the North Carolina airport . Nashville was different. WestJet entered the market in May 2023, providing the city pair's first-ever flights. Air Canada arrived two years later. WestJet pulled out in June 2026, followed by Canada's flag carrier three months later.

The same period was used to examine cuts to Air Canada's domestic map. Air Canada flew between Toronto Pearson and Yellowknife, in the Northwest Territories not far from the Arctic Circle, until August 2026. This year, the A319 (Rouge) and 737 MAX 8 (mainline and Rouge) were primarily used, although the A320 (mainline and Rouge) and A321 (Rouge) appeared too.

The long route, which covered 1,655 nautical miles (3,065 km) each way, launched in 2023. Flights materialized around 19 months after the debut of Air North. Perhaps unusually, Air Canada flew on a year-round basis, although winter frequencies and capacity was, of course, significantly lower than during the summer.

title_en: CFM Built A Jet Engine So Large That It Forced A Redesign Of The Jet It Powers
title_zh: CFM 制造的喷气发动机太大，以至于不得不重新设计其所驱动的喷气式飞机
summary: The engineering compromises that brought a 1960s jet into the 21st Century.
summary_zh: 工程上的妥协将 20 世纪 60 年代的喷气式飞机带入了 21 世纪。
body_en: Luke Diaz is a freelance military writer with experience with active duty experience in the US Navy as well as defense and industrial engineering. He is a former Naval Flight Officer who performed tactical air control on the carrier-based E-2 Hawkeye.

CFM International did not arbitrarily build an oversized engine. When Airbus announced the A320neo family featuring ultra-efficient, large-diameter engines, the CFM LEAP-1A and Pratt & Whitney GTF, airlines demanded a matching fuel-efficient option from the American maker. Boeing demanded a high-bypass turbofan to compete with Airbus, forcing the engine maker to deliver the LEAP-1B. Rather than spending years and billions of dollars building a clean-sheet, modern airplane from scratch, Boeing chose to modify the existing 737 Next Generation (NG) airframe.

The original 1960s Boeing 737 was intentionally designed to sit very low to the ground. In the MAX, Boeing attempted to fit 2010s engine technology onto an airframe originally designed in the 1960s, in stark contrast to its competitor. While CFM actually shrunk the 737 MAX's engine fan to 69 inches (175 cm), compared to the 78-inch (198 cm) for Airbus, it was still far too large for the existing 737 airframe.

Moving the heavy, wide engines upward and forward meant that during specific high-altitude, high-angle-of-attack maneuvers, the engine nacelles acted like mini-wings. To counteract the aerodynamics and ensure the MAX handled exactly like older 737 models, Boeing implemented the Maneuvering Characteristics Augmentation System software. MCAS was intended to operate in the background and autonomously push the nose back down, which ultimately became the focal point of the subsequent 737 MAX design crisis.
America's Low-Slung Jetliner: Legacy And An Airframe Dilemma

In April 1967, Boeing introduced the 737, which had a low fuselage and short landing gear for ease of ground crew access and was intended for tiny airports with minimal equipment needs. Pratt & Whitney JT8D engines, which fit neatly beneath the wing, were used in early variants. Wider fans were more cost-effective, but they also added weight and drag; thus, the need for greater fuel economy created problems.

When Boeing began planning the 737-100 and -200 in 1964, the aviation world looked vastly different. Jet travel was transitioning to smaller cities, and the primary design objective was to build a self-sufficient aircraft. To pull off the ultimate trick of building virtually new planes while legally keeping them registered under the exact same 1967 type certificate, Boeing used a clever strategy for both the NG and the MAX.

In the 1990s, Boeing engineered a larger modern wing, computer-controlled engines, and digital flight screens. However, to keep the planes operationally identical, engineers programmed those advanced digital screens to display retro, analog-style dials and preserved the mechanical overhead switch layout. Pilots could step into the advanced NG and fly it using the exact same muscle memory and procedures as the 1980s Classic models without setting foot in a simulator.

The 2010s 737 MAX repeated this illusion but pushed it past physical limits. To fit massive, ultra-efficient LEAP-1B engines onto the low-slung frame, Boeing moved the engines higher and further forward on the wing. Boeing promised airlines that any pilot flying an NG could transition to a MAX by doing nothing more than an iPad course. To legally satisfy the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) that the MAX was identical to the older 737 NG, Boeing had to present the new plane as having no major behavioral differences.
The Hamster Pouch: Nacelle Cantilevers & Wing Geometry

The 'hamster pouch' engine casing designed for the 1984 Boeing 737-300 is the exact mechanical ancestor of the MAX crisis. It represents the very first time Boeing chose to patch over a fundamental physical limitation with a clever, compromising workaround. When the Boeing 737-300 made its debut in February 1984 with the CFM56-3 engine mounted ahead of the wing, it represented a major engineering change.

The engine's bypass ratio dropped from 24,000 to 20,000 pounds of thrust as a result of this move, which also produced a flat-bottom nacelle known as the hamster pouch and a smaller fan. The MAX initiative was started in 2011 as the need for fuel efficiency increased and the design's shortcomings became apparent. When airlines demanded efficient, wider turbofan engines in the 1980s, Boeing encountered the exact same obstacle they would face decades later: the 1960s fuselage sat too close to the ground.

By the time the 2010s arrived , the required engines had grown so colossally large that flattening the bottom of the casing was no longer enough. Airbus gave CFM a massive 78-inch (198 cm) canvas for the A320neo because the A320 airframe sat high off the ground. Boeing, demanding the exact same thermodynamic efficiency, forced CFM to scale the LEAP engine down to a highly constrained fan for the MAX just so it wouldn't scrape the runway.

To gain clearance, Boeing had to physically relocate the entire engine forward and upward, completely corrupting the airplane's aerodynamics and causing the nose to pitch up. Having run out of room for physical hardware workarounds like the hamster pouch engine housing shape, Boeing turned to a digital workaround instead. The severe, forward-cantilevered placement introduced intense physical loads on the wing structure and created the exact nose-up pitch characteristics that Boeing's MCAS software was secretly built to mask.
How CFM Shrank The LEAP: Aerodynamic Side Effects

The A320neo's LEAP-1A engine, which has a bigger fan, taller landing gear, and a greater bypass ratio than the 737's rejected LEAP 1B, is an example of what CFM might have created with more space. Because it requires less thrust, the LEAP 1B has a redesigned low-pressure turbine construction, a lower bypass ratio, and less weight while maintaining the sophisticated core of its predecessor.

After much discussion, Boeing decided to go with a bigger fan in order to increase efficiency. However, this choice created problems for the airframe, requiring the nacelles to be moved, which altered flight dynamics and potentially conflicted with federal stall regulation standards.

CFM International upgraded the low-pressure turbine of the LEAP-1B engine from seven stages to five in order to lower the weight of the turbofan core in response to the strict design requirements of the MAX. In spite of the heavier engine housing of the CFM56-7B, developers used lightweight titanium alloys and ceramic matrix composites to improve thermodynamic efficiency.
body_zh: 卢克·迪亚兹 (Luke Diaz) 是一位自由军事作家，拥有在美国海军以及国防和工业工程领域服役的现役经验。他是一名前海军飞行军官，曾在舰载 E-2 鹰眼上执行战术空中控制。

CFM国际公司并没有随意打造超大发动机。当空客宣布 A320neo 系列采用超高效、大直径发动机、CFM LEAP-1A 和普惠 GTF 时，航空公司要求这家美国制造商提供匹配的燃油效率选项。波音公司需要高涵道比涡轮风扇发动机来与空中客车公司竞争，迫使这家发动机制造商交付 LEAP-1B。波音公司没有花费数年时间和数十亿美元从头开始建造一架全新的现代化飞机，而是选择修改现有的 737 下一代 (NG) 机身。
最初的 20 世纪 60 年代波音 737 被有意设计为离地非常低。在 MAX 中，波音试图将 2010 年代的发动机技术应用到最初设计于 1960 年代的机身上，这与竞争对手形成鲜明对比。虽然 CFM 实际上将 737 MAX 的发动机风扇缩小至 69 英寸（175 厘米），但与空客的 78 英寸（198 厘米）相比，对于现有 737 机身来说仍然太大。
将重型、宽大的发动机向上和向前移动意味着在特定的高空、大迎角机动过程中，发动机短舱的作用就像迷你机翼一样。为了抵消空气动力学影响并确保 MAX 的操控性能与旧型 737 型号完全相同，波音公司实施了机动特性增强系统软件。 MCAS 的目的是在后台运行并自动将机头推回原位，这最终成为随后 737 MAX 设计危机的焦点。
美国低吊喷气式客机：遗留问题和机身困境
1967 年 4 月，波音推出 737，该机型机身较低，起落架较短，便于地勤人员出入，适用于设备需求极少的小型机场。普拉特·惠特尼 JT8D 发动机巧妙地安装在机翼下方，用于早期型号。更宽的风扇更具成本效益，但它们也增加了重量和阻力；因此，对提高燃油经济性的需求产生了问题。
当波音公司于 1964 年开始规划 737-100 和 -200 时，航空世界看起来截然不同。喷气式飞机旅行正在向较小的城市过渡，主要设计目标是建造一架自给自足的飞机。为了实现建造几乎全新飞机的终极技巧，同时在完全相同的 1967 年型号证书下合法注册它们，波音公司对 NG 和 MAX 都采用了巧妙的策略。
20 世纪 90 年代，波音设计了更大的现代化机翼、计算机控制的发动机和数字飞行屏幕。然而，为了保持飞机的操作相同，工程师对这些先进的数字屏幕进行了编程，以显示复古的模拟式表盘，并保留了机械顶部开关布局。飞行员可以进入先进的 NG 并使用与 20 世纪 80 年代经典型号完全相同的肌肉记忆和程序来驾驶它，而无需踏入模拟器。

2010 年的 737 MAX 重复了这种错觉，但突破了物理极限。为了将大型、超高效的 LEAP-1B 发动机安装到低悬挂的框架上，波音公司将发动机移至机翼上更高、更靠前的位置。波音公司向航空公司承诺，任何驾驶 NG 飞机的飞行员只需通过 iPad 课程即可过渡到 MAX。为了合法地让美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 相信 MAX 与旧款 737 NG 相同，波音公司必须证明这款新飞机在行为上没有重大差异。
仓鼠袋：机舱悬臂和机翼几何形状
为 1984 年波音 737-300 设计的“仓鼠袋”发动机外壳正是 MAX 危机的机械祖先。这代表着波音公司第一次选择通过一种巧妙的、妥协的解决方法来修补基本的物理限制。当波音 737-300 于 1984 年 2 月首次亮相时，CFM56-3 发动机安装在机翼前方，这代表了一项重大的工程变革。
由于这一举措，发动机的涵道比推力从 24,000 磅下降到 20,000 磅，还产生了一个称为仓鼠袋的平底机舱和一个较小的风扇。随着对燃油效率的需求增加以及设计缺陷变得明显，MAX 计划于 2011 年启动。当航空公司在 20 世纪 80 年代需要高效、更宽的涡扇发动机时，波音公司遇到了几十年后面临的完全相同的障碍：1960 年代的机身离地面太近。
到了 2010 年代，所需的发动机已经变得非常大，以至于压平外壳底部已经不够了。空客为 A320neo 提供了 CFM 一块巨大的 78 英寸（198 厘米）画布，因为 A320 机身离地很高。波音公司要求完全相同的热力学效率，迫使 CFM 将 LEAP 发动机缩小为 MAX 的高度受限风扇，这样它就不会刮伤跑道。
为了获得许可，波音公司必须将整个发动机向前和向上重新定位，从而完全破坏了飞机的空气动力学性能并导致机头向上倾斜。由于没有足够的空间来容纳像仓鼠袋发动机外壳形状这样的物理硬件解决方案，波音公司转而采用数字解决方案。严格的前悬臂布置给机翼结构带来了强烈的物理负载，并产生了精确的机头向上俯仰特性，而波音公司的 MCAS 软件正是为了掩盖这些特性而秘密构建的。
CFM 如何缩小 LEAP：空气动力学副作用
A320neo 的 LEAP-1A 发动机比 737 废弃的 LEAP 1B 拥有更大的风扇、更高的起落架和更大的涵道比，是 CFM 可能创造更多空间的一个例子。由于需要较小的推力，LEAP 1B 具有重新设计的低压涡轮结构、较低的涵道比和较轻的重量，同时保留了其前身的复杂核心。
经过多次讨论，波音决定使用更大的风扇以提高效率。然而，这种选择给机身带来了问题，需要移动短舱，这改变了飞行动力，并可能与联邦失速监管标准相冲突。
CFM International将LEAP-1B发动机的低压涡轮从七级升级为五级，以降低涡扇核心的重量，以应对MAX严格的设计要求。尽管 CFM56-7B 的发动机外壳较重，但开发人员仍使用轻质钛合金和陶瓷基复合材料来提高热力学效率。

title_en: Global Airlines Liquidating: The Senseless A380 Dream Finally Dies
title_zh: 全球航空公司清算：毫无意义的 A380 梦想最终破灭
summary: Over the past few years, I’ve extensively covered Global Airlines, the strange “airline startup” that had a single Airbus A380, with which it wanted to bring back the “golden age” of travel. The carrier’s A380 has been parked since the spring of 2025, and just
summary_zh: 在过去的几年里，我广泛报道了环球航空公司，这是一家奇怪的“航空公司初创公司”，拥有一架空客 A380，它希望通过这架飞机
body_en: Over the past few years, I’ve extensively covered Global Airlines , the strange “airline startup” that had a single Airbus A380, with which it wanted to bring back the “golden age” of travel. The carrier’s A380 has been parked since the spring of 2025, and just several months ago, I covered how the company faced several winding up petitions . Well, there’s now an update, which seems long overdue…
Global Airlines given winding up orders by court

Public records in the UK show that Global Airlines has finally been given winding up orders , which is the equivalent of liquidation. This is in response to a petition that was filed on May 29, 2026, and a court approved that order on November 4, 2026. This has only been added to public records today, as there seems to be a one week period between when these decisions are made, and when they’re published for the public.

This means that a government officer from the Insolvency Service will now become the liquidator, and take control of the company, investigate its affairs and the conduct of directors, and collect whatever assets still exist for creditors. This means that the directors no longer have control of the company.

What’s amazing about this entire story is that in the spring of 2025, the company actually operated two roundtrip flights to New York out of Europe , for reasons that most of us couldn’t really make sense of. For that matter, this was part of a wet lease agreement with Portuguese charter company Hi-Fly, given that Global Airlines lacked its own operating certificate.

James Asquith, founder of Global Airlines, gate crashes travel guru Simon Calder's interview with Mike Graham. @james_asquith : "Did you get a cupcake?" @Iromg | @SimonCalder pic.twitter.com/etMVj1TcPu

Shortly after the A380 operated those flights, it entered long term storage , as it needed to undergo heavy maintenance, which costs millions of dollars. The company’s founder, James Asquith, had insisted that the reason the plane was parked for so long was due to delays with being able to get heavy maintenance.
Just months ago, Asquith suggested that the airline would be flying to the Maldives before the end of 2026, despite no progress having been made on the heavy maintenance front.
A post shared by Robyn Asquith (@robynasquith)
The Global Airlines story will make a great documentary

Obviously on the surface, the whole Global Airlines thing sounds a bit odd. But let me simply say that the public knows only a tiny fraction of what was really going on here. That’s true both in terms of what Asquith was showing investors to get them onboard with the concept, and also what he claimed the goals for the company were.

My skepticism with this concept wasn’t because I don’t like to see other people succeed, or because I’m against innovation, or anything like that. Instead, it’s because things aren’t always what they seem, and when you’re raising millions of dollars of other people’s money and selling them a dream, there has to be some chance of that actually becoming a reality.
Keep in mind that in 2025, Asquith appeared on The Times’ 40 richest people under 40 list , which claimed he had a net worth of £183 million, making him richer than Adele. Right.

I’d encourage those who just went along with Asquith to be a little introspective here. For example, when you have publications like SimpleFlying that publish things about Global Airlines without even an ounce of skepticism, and then you have people like Captain Chris who latch on to people like Asquith as if they’re Richard Branson (which he literally compared him to, while pointing out that he was proving the doubters wrong), that’s a problem.
A post shared by Captain Chris | Aviation Life (@captainchris)

Many people lost many millions of dollars on this venture. Now, I’d also encourage them to perhaps be a bit more careful next time. And if you just want to make a donation to someone with no expectation of any return, I’m also happy to wire you my bank account details. 😉

It’s the end of the road (or runway) for Global Airlines, as the A380 “airline” has had its winding up petition approved, meaning the company will now be liquidated. It was only a matter of time before this was going to happen, so I don’t think anyone will be surprised. Hopefully one day the entire story can come to light…
What do you make of Global Airlines liquidating?
body_zh: 在过去的几年里，我广泛报道了环球航空公司，这是一家奇怪的“航空公司初创公司”，拥有一架空客 A380，它希望通过这架飞机带回旅行的“黄金时代”。该航空公司的 A380 自 2025 年春季以来一直处于停放状态，就在几个月前，我报道了该公司如何面临几起清盘申请。好吧，现在有一个更新，这似乎姗姗来迟......
环球航空公司被法院发出清盘令
英国的公开记录显示，环球航空公司终于收到了清盘令，相当于清算。这是对 2026 年 5 月 29 日提交的请愿书的回应，法院于 2026 年 11 月 4 日批准了该命令。该命令直到今天才被添加到公共记录中，因为从做出这些决定到向公众发布这些决定之间似乎有一周的时间。
这意味着破产服务局的政府官员现在将成为清算人，并控制公司，调查其事务和董事的行为，并为债权人收回仍存在的所有资产。这意味着董事不再拥有公司的控制权。
整个故事的令人惊奇之处在于，在 2025 年春天，该公司实际上运营了两趟从欧洲飞往纽约的往返航班，其原因我们大多数人都无法真正理解。就此而言，鉴于环球航空公司缺乏自己的运营证书，这是与葡萄牙包机公司 Hi-Fly 湿租协议的一部分。
全球航空公司创始人詹姆斯·阿斯奎斯（James Asquith）在登机口撞坏了旅行大师西蒙·考尔德（Simon Calder）对迈克·格雷厄姆（Mike Graham）的采访。 @james_asquith：“你拿到纸杯蛋糕了吗？” @Iromg | @SimonCalder pic.twitter.com/etMVj1TcPu
A380 执飞这些航班后不久，就进入长期存放状态，因为它需要进行大量维护，维护费用达数百万美元。该公司创始人詹姆斯·阿斯奎斯坚称，这架飞机停放这么长时间的原因是无法进行大规模维护。
就在几个月前，阿斯奎斯表示该航空公司将在 2026 年底前开通飞往马尔代夫的航班，尽管在大规模维护方面尚未取得任何进展。
Robyn Asquith (@robynasquith) 分享的帖子
全球航空公司的故事将成为一部精彩的纪录片
显然，从表面上看，整个环球航空公司的事情听起来有点奇怪。但我只想说，公众只知道这里真正发生的事情的一小部分。无论是阿斯奎斯向投资者展示的让他们接受这一概念的内容，还是他所声称的公司目标，都是如此。
我对这个概念的怀疑并不是因为我不喜欢看到其他人成功，或者因为我反对创新，或者类似的事情。相反，这是因为事情并不总是像看上去的那样，当你筹集其他人数百万美元的资金并向他们推销梦想时，必须有机会真正成为现实。
请记住，2025年，阿斯奎斯出现在《泰晤士报》40位40岁以下最富有的人名单中，该名单声称他的净资产为1.83亿英镑，使他比阿黛尔更富有。正确的。
我鼓励那些赞同阿斯奎斯的人在这里进行一些反省。例如，当你有像 SimpleFlying 这样的出版物，在没有一丝怀疑的情况下发布有关全球航空公司的信息，然后你有像克里斯机长这样的人，他们紧紧抓住像阿斯奎斯这样的人，就好像他们是理查德·布兰森（他确实将他与理查德·布兰森进行了比较，同时指出他正在证明怀疑者是错误的），那就是一个问题。
克里斯船长分享的帖子 |航空生活 (@captainchris)
许多人在这次冒险中损失了数百万美元。现在，我也鼓励他们下次要更加小心一点。如果您只是想向某人捐款而不期望任何回报，我也很乐意向您电汇我的银行帐户详细信息。 😉
这是环球航空公司道路（或跑道）的尽头，因为 A380“航空公司”的清盘申请已获得批准，这意味着该公司现在将进行清算。这一切的发生只是时间问题，所以我认为任何人都不会感到惊讶。希望有一天整个故事能够真相大白……

title_en: Why Business Class Suites With Doors Need Additional Aircraft Safety Certification
title_zh: 为什么带门的商务舱套房需要额外的飞机安全认证
summary: Business class seats are more private today than they have ever been before, though that has come at the expense of rigorous safety certification.
summary_zh: 如今的商务舱座椅比以往任何时候都更加私密，尽管这是以严格的安全认证为代价的。
body_en: Airline and Airport Management Graduate, Student Commercial Pilot and Commercial Aviation Writer.

The introduction of sliding privacy doors into modern business class cabins has completely changed the premium passenger experience, moving from open reverse-herringbone layouts into private, cocoon-like suites. So many flyers celebrate the addition of personal doors on flagships like United Airlines' new Boeing 787-9 Polaris suites or American Airlines' Flagship configurations, though in the background, strict regulations have to be met. A suite door is not just a comfort feature, as it is also a barrier between a passenger and an emergency exit, drawing intense scrutiny from aviation authorities.

Business class suite doors therefore need extensive additional safety certification to satisfy the demands of global safety authorities. From 16g crash testing to strict 90-second emergency egress mandates, introducing doors into the cabin requires special exemptions, meticulous testing, and regulatory approvals that frequently lag behind the delivery of the aircraft itself.

Aviation regulators once evaluated premium cabin seating primarily through the lens of traditional structural integrity, restraint systems, and standard evacuation pathways. Traditional open lie-flat business class seats presented straightforward compliance paths because flight attendants and evacuating passengers had clear, unobstructed lines of sight and immediate access to aisles. When manufacturers began designing suites with doors, however, these established certification frameworks proved insufficient to address the new variables introduced by partitioned personal spaces.

The core regulatory concern centered on emergency evacuation under worst-case conditions. According to Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) mandates, any commercial aircraft must be capable of a full evacuation within 90 seconds in total darkness , with half of the emergency exits blocked and amid simulated passenger panic. A closed or jammed sliding door at the start of an emergency could potentially impede a disoriented or panicked passenger from exiting their suite. Consequently, regulators need to be able to see extensive documentation and demonstration proving that a suite door's design, latching mechanism, and breakaway features will not meaningfully delay egress.

Furthermore, cabin doors are governed by strict regulatory classifications, as detailed by Sofema Aviation . Because standard airworthiness rules did not anticipate partial-height sliding doors dividing passenger seats from exit paths, airlines and seat manufacturers must regularly apply for regulatory exemptions or special conditions. These tailored requirements impose rigorous oversight on how doors operate, so that the pursuit of luxury never compromises baseline aviation safety.

Basic egress clearance is just the beginning, as suite doors need to withstand extreme forces and operational stress during flight to get certification. Every premium seat model incorporating a door is subjected to punishing dynamic 16g sled tests , which simulate the immense G-forces of a survivable crash landing. During these tests, the door structure, locking pins, and track mechanisms need to remain intact. This is to show that structural flexing of the airframe does not jam the door shut and trap a passenger inside their suite during an emergency.

In addition to crash dynamics, modern cabin engineering also must account for rapid decompression and airflow management. As highlighted in Simple Flying analysis , tightly sealed suite doors can alter cabin pressure equalization and oxygen mask deployment patterns during a rapid decompression event. Regulators need to see proof that air can flow freely between the enclosed suite and the main cabin volume so that passengers are not starved of supplemental oxygen or subjected to dangerous pressure differentials if hull integrity is compromised at altitude.

The rigorous engineering demands mean that seat development cycles are frequently prolonged. When Qatar Airways partnered with Adient to develop the Ascent seat for its 787-9 fleet, achieving regulatory compliance for the sliding door mechanism contributed significantly to a two-year program delay , culminating in FAA certification being completed in January 2021.

Even after a suite door successfully passes structural crash tests and evacuation trials, its operational use is still heavily restricted during critical phases of flight. FAA exemption documents and cabin safety guidelines dictate that suite doors must be locked in the open position during taxi, takeoff, and landing (TTL). The reason is that flight attendants need to have an unobstructed view of all seated passengers and all exit pathways should be entirely clear during the most statistically vulnerable phases of flight.
